::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 24. 1865  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55384 (1): P. 291
:::

Dear Miss Yonge	
[I](people/person_939.qmd) am writing to [Mrs Vaughan](people/person_1929.qmd) & will tell her with how much pleasure I consent to her using the story from [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd). I will remind you when we reprint, that you may give us the additional story. 

I don’t think I ever congratulated you on the marvellous good scotch you give us in the [Clever Woman](cmy_books/cmybook_58.qmd).[^1] I, a western man, from the Land of Burns, claim a classical purity in my own Scotch taste and could detect no flaw.

When you have any ['Bethlehem'](organizations/other_177.qmd) done I would rather like to have, say a chapter to make experiments in type to.

The [Sunday Library](organizations/other_145.qmd) scheme, could I have no doubt, be arranged in the way you indicate. My feeling that substantially no one whom I would wish to help in it, would disagree with your feeling. I am sure by dwelling in all cases on the <u>life</u>, there will be so much the less chance of straying from the light. But the organisation will want a little help. I shall be so grateful for guidance even if you do not feel free to assume the responsibility. I am anxious however, that [Mrs Gatty](people/person_549.qmd) should not be asked, at least as from me, and for this reason. She has published with my excellent friend [George Bell](people/person_1930.qmd) for many years. I would like exceedingly to keep up the old loyal policy between author & publisher so far as I could, and this would be like poaching on a friends preserves. I think I can safely say I have never done so yet. In a scheme which I want to do good I would like to avoid it. Otherwise I admire her & shall much [*illegible*]. [Miss Keary](people/person_793.qmd) tells me about your ['Goslings'](organizations/other_104.qmd). Any <u>very good</u> one I would certainly not object [to]. I rather fancy new brain. But we will have time to talk over all this.

Have you quite decided on the title of your story for the [Mag](organizations/other_78.qmd). '[The Dove in the Eagle’s Nest](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd)' is slightly sentimental. I dont know that it is any worse for that. But perhaps a somewhat simpler one would do better.

Yours very faithfully
A. Macmillan

---

[^1]: In *The Clever Woman of the Family* there is a housekeeper who speaks broad Scottish.
